questions.q: How does OneLake security differ from a workspace role?
options: OneLake security is item-level, controlling which rows and columns are visible; a workspace role only gates access to the item itself
OneLake security and workspace roles are two names for exactly the same setting
OneLake security replaces workspace roles entirely — workspace roles no longer matter once it's enabled
OneLake security only applies to Power BI reports, never to lakehouses or warehouses
questions.explain: Workspace roles (Lesson 5) gate access to the Fabric item itself. OneLake security is a finer-grained layer inside the item that controls exactly which rows and columns a role's members can see.

questions.q: Where do you start creating a OneLake security role?
options: A lakehouse item's "..." menu, under "Manage OneLake security (preview)"
The tenant-level admin portal's Domains page
A capacity's settings page
Only through the Power BI report's file menu
questions.explain: The entry point shown in the lesson is a lakehouse's "..." menu, which includes "Manage OneLake security (preview)" alongside other management options.

questions.q: What is row security in OneLake, concretely?
options: A SQL WHERE-clause filter that determines which rows a role's members can see
A list of usernames allowed to log into the workspace
A setting that hides entire tables from everyone
A separate password required to open the lakehouse
questions.explain: Row security is defined as an actual SQL WHERE clause: "Show data to members of your role if the following rules apply," evaluated against the selected table.

questions.q: Where is OneLake security actually enforced?
options: Wherever the data is read from — a notebook, the SQL analytics endpoint, or a Power BI report built on top
Only inside the Fabric web portal's item view
Only when exporting data to Excel
It is not enforced anywhere; it is purely documentation
questions.explain: The lesson stresses that OneLake security travels with the data — it's enforced wherever it's read from, not just through the Fabric UI.

questions.q: On the New role wizard's Data step, what must you choose before row or column security rules can apply to specific tables?
options: Selected data, rather than All data, so specific tables/folders can be picked and ruled on individually
Nothing — row and column security apply automatically to every table in the workspace
A capacity region for the role
A domain the role belongs to
questions.explain: The Data step offers All data or Selected data with an Edit button; choosing Selected data and picking specific tables is what makes table-specific row/column rules possible.
